evidence: Runnable single-flake calculations: Mitra and co-authors' (1990) wind-tunnel-based melting model as Frick and co-authors (2013) give it, McSnow's aggregates and fall speeds, the rain solver's drops, through the archived air of the design-climate CM1 boxes; checked on Earth against observed and computed melting depths; no lunar validation.
reading_rule: Depths are metres below each column's freezing level; heights are metres above the box's surface (sea level for the sea box, the box's own ground for the land box). Budgets are fractions of the snow mass flux arriving at the freezing level; heat is W/m2 for each mm/h of that snowfall (water equivalent). Composites take the snow-weighted median of temperature and vapour pressure at each depth below the freezing level; moist and dry take the 90th and 10th percentiles of vapour pressure. Sampled columns are drawn by their snow at the freezing level.
assumptions: Still air: the boxes' vertical motions are left out.
Flakes fall alone: no aggregation, collision or breakup of flakes below the freezing level.
A flake melts to one drop and drops fall alone; a drop above its stability screen breaks into eight drops of half its diameter, again until they hold together.

The melting flake's vapour comes from exposed ice in proportion to the ice's share of its mass; that split moves the record between sublimation, melting and evaporation and leaves the masses and the heat taken from the air unchanged.
Vapour diffusivity is the rain solver's, Massman's (1998) measured fit since 25 October.
Gravity holds its surface value through the column, as in CM1.
